release_review.summary: Epoch 23 pairs Runtime and Desktop on Flower confirmed/estimated context snapshots from published Floret v7.16.1. Existing autonomous computer targets, authorization, Activity, and InputRequired contracts remain enforced. The unreleased v0.13.0 minimum window and product schema 9 remain unchanged.
checked_surfaces: Provider preparation freezes the exact OpenAI Responses/Chat, Gemini-compatible Chat, Moonshot and Anthropic body before estimation and dispatch. Published Floret v7.16.1 owns model-aware offline text and media estimates; opaque Desktop/platform sources retain explicitly generic input estimates. No Runtime Service, Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup report, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH bootstrap, context snapshot or storage wire shape changes; compatibility epoch 23 remains valid. Canonical usage, permissions, reasoning, tool aliases, signatures and overflow recovery retain their existing ownership. Floret derives Ask User waits from committed control calls so a late duplicate cannot reopen an answer; no host lifecycle workaround or storage migration is introduced.

Flower bootstrap, live workspace SSE and reconnect carry separate confirmed and estimate samples. Desktop and Env App show the last native measurement with a previous-request label while current prediction controls risk. Empty snapshots clear samples on model/budget changes and successful compaction. Runtime Service, Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance and SSH runtime bootstrap require epoch 23; epoch 22 is admitted for upgrade only. No Floret schema or product database migration is introduced.

Flower computer.targets and computer.select_target use Runtime-issued thread-scoped candidates. UI and model share selection, connected personal browsers precede managed pages, new conversations create independent task tabs, and popup progress never replays an executed action. Desktop route allowlists, connection UI, Runtime Service, Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance and SSH runtime bootstrap require epoch 23. Epoch 21 is admitted for upgrade only. Current grants, Stop, private control, stale identity, occupancy and unknown effects remain enforced; no Floret API or database migration is added. Chrome webNavigation creation events supply actual popup source tab IDs; tab grouping metadata is not routing authority.

Flower preserves natural-language invocation intent and safe inputs independently of results through live updates, canonical history and restart. Desktop and Env App decode inputs, rows_provided, language and truncated; published Floe Webapp v0.56.11 owns localized accessible code copy feedback. Runtime Service, Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance and SSH runtime bootstrap negotiate epoch 23. Upgrade admission includes epoch 20; old peers cannot silently accept the extended strict Activity contract. No historical Activity backfill or Floret domain schema change is introduced.

Computer connections use authenticated Runtime APIs for managed profiles, explicit CDP tabs, and same-device Chrome Native Messaging. The Runtime remains the target and resource owner; Floret v7 retains canonical tool effects, InputRequired continuation and unknown-effect terminal state. Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance UI and SSH runtime bootstrap require epoch 23. Browser execution and Native Messaging use protocol 4; native helpers retain protocol 3; inventory and isolated script helpers retain protocol 2; semantic batches share 30-second, 50-operation and 64-MiB guest limits. Product schema 8-to-9 adds task origins, applications and foreground authorization without modifying Floret storage. Live Stage sampling is independent of model screenshot selection.

File previews consume published Floe Webapp v0.56.11 content-box observation and fit geometry. PDF, DOCX, images and media retain existing file authorization and Workbench input ownership while correcting fit modes, scrolling and asynchronous rendering. Real floating-window, mobile and Workbench tests cover resizing and DPR 1/2. These renderer-only changes add no Runtime Service, Desktop bridge, storage or transport fields and retain their existing wire shapes within compatibility epoch 23.

Workbench composition materials, direct editing, all-theme visual refinement, and bounded Ask Flower windows consume published Floe v0.56.11 without adding theme IPC fields, changing selection schema version 1, or altering Runtime Service protocol. Desktop native first paint, renderer theme synchronization and isolated Web Service controls retain their existing theme schema within the epoch 23 Runtime access window. Welcome processing actions and Flower running text opt into the published Floe progress shimmer using existing states, with no new IPC, transport, storage, or user-setting fields.

HTTP is explicit through the published Flowersec 5.2.2 HTTPDirect profile and Floe Webapp 0.56.11 lifecycle APIs. HTTPS certificate and private-loopback validation remain fail closed. ReDevPlugin 3.0.32 and Floeterm 0.19.2 preserve standard SHA-256 integrity on HTTP. Startup reports publish only actual public URLs; protected bridge hello carries public URLs separately from its private transport token. Desktop settings separate current connection, access scope, password, protocol, and next-start inputs. Local Runtime outlives the initiating Desktop; URL clients have no lifecycle authority.

Floret v7.11.2 preserves host media identifiers through Activity sanitization, durable replay, and model request snapshots. Flower resolves computer_frame resource_ref values through its authenticated thread media route; Desktop carries PNG bytes over the existing authorized request IPC. The media-only floating viewer preserves decoded pixels until replacement frames finish loading. The compatibility handshake requires epoch 19 so a pre-media Desktop cannot silently drop references or fail its strict Activity decoder.

Flower settings in Desktop and Env App use the same administrator-only read-only model_catalog endpoint and offline generated catalog. Brand selection persists exclusions and sparse overrides; Runtime startup atomically converts old profiles without changing current or thread models. OpenRouter keeps explicit selection, Ollama resolves installed tool models without a persistent inventory, and per-model image input includes prepared DeepSeek Vision through published Floret v7.11.2. Gemini credentials, effort/budget controls, image input, and tool thought signatures use the existing provider boundary. Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, and SSH runtime bootstrap negotiate epoch 19 before allowing profile exchange.

Floret v7.11.2 public inspection, WAL snapshots, deferred Host activation, and restore preparation own canonical storage and execution. Product and read-state stores share the readiness generation; backing_up and restoring remain Flower-only maintenance states in Env App, Desktop, Runtime Service, and sys.ping. Administrator-confirmed restoration uses a durable complete-set replacement journal, preserves prior data and queued inputs, and invalidates old execution and approval. New user submissions fetch the storage generation; persisted outbox retries retain their original generation and remain copyable after rejection. The flower-title-generation-v1 title contract and all transport review surfaces remain required.

Flower HTTP lists, details, and live summaries carry Floret title_generation. Desktop and Env App require the same canonical title contract; the existing compatibility handshake rejects older epoch combinations. Title text, status, and generation share one ThreadCache summary owner independently of runtime views.

DeepSeek uses the published Floret stateless Responses gateway, catalog-owned search availability with unsupported built-in tools rejected, and existing supplemental-context privacy fences without changing the Desktop or Runtime protocol. Redeven consumes published github.com/floegence/floret/v7 v7.16.1 with GOWORK=off and exact module checksums; every production Agent binds one immutable RunLabels snapshot at construction so fresh execution and continuations share Floret's provider-host injection point, while provider admission and policy refresh never rebind the admitted permission snapshot; committed final provider usage carries canonical whole-thread cache token totals through the live event boundary without a downstream ledger, while projected requests preserve the last confirmed totals; Floret-native web_fetch owns secure public-text fetching, parsing, output policy, and typed Activity with a bounded preview while ignoring page icons, and Redeven owns current product authorization plus one Searching indicator that animates only while the fetch is running; runtime startup atomically converges legacy UTF-8 tool-result Raw data, exact RunID identity, and every dispatching, retrying, or unknown effect into one typed terminal failure before the Host is available and removes terminal forked Effect Attempt history only when source-thread ancestry and execution identity are verified; canonical Effect results converge from one committed entry with valid UTF-8 text, segmented records preserve active-turn recovery without whole-state rewrites, published SQLite maintenance reclaims eligible free pages before the single runtime open, root inventory supplies summary-only list projection, cumulative typed Activity preserves terminal call descriptions through results and restart, additive terminal operation and safe byte/cursor facts keep every terminal call inspectable without exposing interactive input, user cancellation records the selected Thread, Turn, and Run before canceling execution, typed SubAgent operation Activity preserves the exact action, ordered targets, counts, and wait timeout through restart; child current views replace only the parent Subagent inventory and never enter the root thread list; admitted child mutations do not perform post-effect List, View, or title calls, user Stop opts into Floret graceful cancellation with one five-second settlement deadline, preserves confirmed tool results and output, and seals late provider, tool, and save-point work after terminal settlement, canonical terminal items replace stream-only text without appending run-level output, stale canonical snapshots cannot replace a newer terminal view, canonical queue and interaction acceptance precedes visible success, unknown effects fail once and cannot be replayed, delete and shutdown fence active subtrees and effect dispatch, migration v2 through v11 remains atomic and fail-closed, verified fork context is rewritten to destination Thread identity without a downstream repair path, ordered views stay monotonic across live updates and restart, new tool history preserves complete Engine-authored call reasoning and hosted assistant fragment boundaries so source and fork continuation survive restart without duplicate calls; existing corrupt history is not rewritten, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access exists

Floret ThreadView.RunID, ThreadItem.RunID, ThreadInteraction.RunID, and RunProgress are the exact execution identity and phase source; Redeven does not infer historical run identity from the current run, TurnID, message content, or a parallel model-I/O stream

Floret v7.11.2 owns append-only canonical context plus full Turn-surface render lineages: forked context takes destination Thread identity from the canonical entry while preserving historical Turn and Run identity; Redeven freezes the persisted model, reasoning, System Prompt, tools, adapter, and context policy at new-Turn admission, treats request model fields only as consistency checks, keeps the original user objective in canonical history, appends mutable environment facts as durable per-turn UserInput.Context snapshots without rewriting an earlier request prefix, and starts each new context policy without the previous model's latest usage while preserving cumulative whole-thread totals
A natural provider stop completes a Flower Turn; ordinary tools continue, ask_user waits and resumes the same immutable surface, and settings or product-version changes affect only a later Turn

Provider history preserves ask_user as one Assistant tool call plus matching Tool result; public answers occur once in that result, secret values remain ephemeral, and provider-context v8 keeps typed historical tool facts stable across later Turns without restoring removed definitions or hashing runtime and journal entry identities

Floret v7.11.2 strictly validates model arguments and allows at most two regeneration attempts with complete canonical call/result pairs. Invalid ask_user arguments do not create an interaction or Activity; UI filtering never removes provider history. Exhaustion retains control_error and generated text with a localized retry action, while projector, storage, and unknown-effect failures remain terminal. Historical control failures cannot create pending input, and Flower rejects missing, null, or empty typed questions before ThreadCache.

Historical tool Activity is projected from persisted canonical presentation without consulting the current registry; removed tools use one neutral safe presentation and are not restored as compatibility definitions

Every Floret Run transition publishes the new exact RunID in preparing before provider dispatch and resets attempt ownership; Redeven forwards preparing, waiting_response, streaming, reasoning, and assistant growth directly without polling, inferred progress, or terminal backfill

Floret v7.11.2 publishes an unresolved approval or user-input interaction together with the matching active projection in one transition: waiting interactions clear run_progress while other active summaries retain it; local waiters are reserved before durable admission so response handling resumes the existing execution without duplicate provider dispatch

Floret v7.11.2 publishes validated command presentation and tool settlement directly from its existing thread actor before output or turn completion. Desktop and Env App consume unchanged ThreadView fields; failed tools default collapsed and retain manual disclosure choices. The additive Cancellation fact binds stop source and exact execution identity across summary, current view, and restart. Flower shows Stopping until canonical settlement, then restores the composer silently or shows an explicit unconfirmed-results warning; stop admission failures remain actionable. Runtime Service protocol, compatibility epoch, and product storage schema are unchanged; Floret owns its automatic domain schema migration.
Floret ThreadService is the only lifecycle boundary for View, Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, PromoteQueued, and Subscribe
Each Floret thread has one in-memory ThreadRuntime owner; its canonical journal is the only durable lifecycle fact source
Redeven persists only product settings, authorization audit, uploads, read state, and the contiguous v1-to-v2 migration import boundary
Redeven handlers authorize and map typed requests without admission receipts, authority barriers, recovery handles, or projection mirrors
Flower uses one workspace SSE, summary/detail-separated ThreadCache, ComposerDraftStore, short-lived IndexedDB TransportOutbox, and LiveTransport
Thread selection never owns execution or reconnects transport; summary updates never overwrite typed detail
Unknown irreversible tool effects terminate their Turn with effect_outcome_unknown and have no replay or retry surface

Redeven consumes only published Flowersec Go and Core v5.2.2 plus Floe Webapp v0.56.11 for both the Desktop shell and Env App, with exact module checksums and no replace, file, link, workspace, portal, sibling checkout, private import, or copied transport implementation

Public Local UI uses explicitly configured HTTP/WS or HTTPS/WSS on one shared public listener with exact Host and Origin admission, one-shot artifacts, isolated concurrent windows, explicit terminal failure, and cleanup of pending authorization, handlers, sessions, and notification sinks; the private Desktop document bridge instead uses the isolated flowersec-private-loopback/1 browser and Go APIs behind exact numeric-loopback and per-process bridge-token admission

Each remote or local accepted session registers the final Flowersec SessionHandlers, RPC, ByteStream, and terminal/live_v1 boundaries directly; outbound terminal notification sinks attach to the established Flowersec RPC peer and detach idempotently when that session ends

Desktop attach and start, CA-free private bridge health, optional public device CA trust, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH runtime bootstrap, same-port public WS/WSS, terminal history recovery, and consecutive Desktop bridge sessions remain covered by focused transport contracts

Flowersec ConnectionController remains the only reconnect owner; secure-session retry uses Floe Webapp replaceConnection so an old asynchronous close cannot overwrite a new controller generation, while Redeven supplies artifact acquisition, authorization, permissions, product RPC handlers, and post-session business recovery without a second reconnect state machine or alternate carrier path

The desktop-placement-http2-v1 boundary remains unchanged. Runtime Service protocol_version is redeven-runtime-v2 at compatibility_epoch 23; Desktop verifies Runtime Service, the redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1 private bridge, Catalog, Local UI, package identity, and a unique managed process before a direct lifecycle operation succeeds
Gateway is an optional access component and never prepares, starts, stops, updates, reinstalls, or supervises a managed Runtime

Published ReDevPlugin 3.0.32 prepares validated installed Worker modules during process startup before an Env App session exists, while authenticated recovery remains the execution authority. The released bounded document cache retains only hash-matched bytes and revalidates trust. Workbench hidden and offscreen first commits, exact-slot retry cleanup, real Desktop runtime restart, and preparation latency are covered without changing Runtime Service protocol, Rust IPC, or plugin author API.

Desktop CodeSpace windows and system-browser openings share the selected EnvironmentSession route and generation-bound Runtime handler. ID-only browser intent mints a single-use entry on an isolated cs-<profile>.localhost origin; Host-only browser cookies never reach Runtime or the editor. Epoch 14 rejects older runtimes that only accept numeric-loopback presentation origins. Entry expiry, HTTP resources, WebSockets, AccessGate, environment disposal, file save and terminal execution are covered without replaying application traffic.

Web Service observation, action capabilities and reviewed plans distinguish missing resources, unavailable inspection and ownership conflicts. Uninstall journals preserve per-resource results; detach atomically archives management and revokes active proxy streams without stopping business processes. Registry portforward_registry_v2 advances from schema 3 to 4 without moving existing resources or changing TemplateSpec v6. All Activity and Workbench entries use the same review drawer and instance resource boundary.

Floret v7.11.2 renders canonical references and accepted context snapshots into the actual provider history, including continuation, retry, fork, restart, and compaction. ResourceRef remains opaque and secret answers remain ephemeral. The contiguous v9-to-v10 migration validates existing records without rewriting historical journal bytes; provider-context v8 establishes an explicit projection boundary. Environment cards distinguish the user-selected device from the tool execution environment and include the existing routing skill at admission. Terminal Activity shows actual result target and execution location without inferring remote execution from a local CLI command. Existing Desktop/Runtime wire shapes and compatibility epoch remain unchanged.

Env App Cloud bootstrap receives only the signed HTTP plugin path and CSRF-header additions from proxy.runtime@2. WebSocket scope, Code App and Port Forward management isolation, Origin and CSRF checks, authenticated channel identity, and session retirement remain enforced. Runtime Service wire protocol and compatibility epoch are unchanged.

Env App idle liveness consumes Floe 0.56.11. Desktop adds a scoped no-argument provider-session renewal IPC for its owning Cloud bootstrap document; main uses existing RCPP open-session and sandbox boot exchange with saved account authorization. Old Desktop peers retain explicit session reopening. Runtime Service wire, compatibility epoch 23, origin/CSRF checks and sandbox cookie lifetime are unchanged.
